summary: scripts/evidence-gc --lock-config turns a protection on the remote's evidence tags (a tag ruleset) off only around its own tag deletions, relocks in a finally that also runs on a signal, checks it is on at the end and raises an alarm for any tag that disappeared or moved outside the plan; scripts/evidence-gc.timer runs it daily as a systemd user unit on a host we hold.

replay.detail: Operator script, unit files and an example config only; no record, signature or verifier rule changes.

schema.detail: New lock config file {"version": 1, "unlock", "relock", "check"}, each an argv list, read by --lock-config; example in scripts/evidence-gc-lock.example.json.

rules.detail: With a lock config, GC deletes notes and migrations first, then the tags inside the window; exit 4 when the protection was found off, is not on at the end, or a tag it did not plan disappeared or moved. Without one it behaves as before.

manual.detail: To schedule GC: copy scripts/evidence-gc-timer to ~/.local/bin, scripts/evidence-gc.service and .timer to ~/.config/systemd/user, the lock config to ~/.config/evidence-gc/lock.json with the ruleset id, then systemctl --user enable --now evidence-gc.timer.

recovery.detail: Disable the timer; --relock-only turns the protection back on.
